# Screw the rack to the bench

A rack that is not screwed down tips forwards when you pull on an open drawer of the top row. Screw each floor
plate to the bench with two wood screws. Choose where the rack goes before you put up the first ladder.

The open drawers hang ahead of the front edge of the base. Unplugging a USB-C cable from a board in an open
top drawer is enough to tip a loose rack over that edge. So is leaning on an open drawer, or pushing a plug
into a board that lies on one.

```{figure} ../img/viewer/rack-side-drawers-out.jpg
:alt: A rack of three rows seen from its right side, every drawer pulled out ahead of the base
:width: 55%

The 3D model from the right, every drawer pulled out. The rack tips over the front edge of its base.
```

## Two screws per floor plate

Each column of bays stands on its own floor plate, so you need two screws per column. Use wood screws
3.5 × 16 with a pan head, each on an M4 washer. They are on the [shopping list](../plan/shopping-list.md), not
in the bill of materials.

The floor plate has bosses on a 30 mm grid, four across and six deep. Use these two:

| Screw | Boss |
|---|---|
| Front | the front row, third boss from the left |
| Rear | the rear row, second boss from the left |

Use bosses with no insert in them: an insert stops the screw. Under bay A1, at the bottom left, the front
screw lands 3.5 mm to the right of the power box.

## When to drive the screws

Drive the two screws of a column once its base brace is on, before the tray of the bottom row goes in. That is
step 4 of [Build the first bay](first-bay.md), and step 3 of
[Add a column or a row](add-a-bay.md#put-up-the-base-of-a-column). Once the bottom tray is in, only a stubby
screwdriver reaches them.

## If you cannot drill the bench

* Screw the floor plates to an MDF board instead. Use one 18 mm thick, as wide as the rack and at least
  500 mm deep. Under a rack of four rows, a board 400 mm deep is not enough.
* If there is a wall behind the rack, tie the rear posts of the top ladders to it with two furniture anti-tip
  straps.

Ballast in the base does not hold a rack down. Nor do printed feet, or a second rack beside it.
